anchors.paper_title: Impact of Biological and Lifestyle Factors on Cognitive Aging and Work Ability in the Dortmund Vital Study: Protocol of an Interdisciplinary, Cross-sectional, and Longitudinal Study
anchors.reason: The Dortmund Vital Study protocol describes the broader multi-domain cohort study the resting-state EEG dataset likely belongs to, but it is not this dataset's own data paper.

metadata.methods_description: Resting-state EEG was recorded in a quiet laboratory with participants seated, using a 64-channel actiCap system (10-20 layout, FCz online reference) and a BrainVision BrainAmp DC amplifier. Sampling rate was 1000 Hz with a 250 Hz online low-pass filter, and impedances were kept below 10 kOhm. Eyes-closed recording always preceded eyes-open recording, and both were done before and after a 2-hour cognitive task block.

funding.funder_name: The Dortmund Vital Study is funded by the institute’s budget (no grant number). Thus, the study design, collection, management, analysis, interpretation of data, writing of the report, and the decision to submit the report for publication is not influenced or biased by any sponsor.
Leibniz Research Centre for Working Environment and Human Factors (IfADo)
